title: Discover recorded changes without inferring the next activity
actor: An engineer joining an existing project
goal: Identify the available current recorded changes and their observed identities so the engineer can explicitly choose which work to inspect.
context: The engineer has project access but has not selected a change or authorized a workflow transition. A fresh checkout may contain the engineering definition without its local operational history.
preconditions: The project context and supported placement configuration are supplied or resolved under the published command contract.

interaction.action: Requests the available current changes in the project.
Returns bounded current candidates with their observed record contracts and revisions, inspected scope, exclusions, and any incomplete or invalid candidates.
Selects a change explicitly for subsequent inspection using those factual results.

expected_outcome: The engineer can distinguish available current work from excluded or problematic material without receiving an invented next activity, implicit selection, or approval.

alternatives.condition: The engineer already knows the desired change.
alternatives.outcome: An explicit change request reports that selected change without enumerating unrelated directories.

alternatives.condition: No current candidate exists in the inspected scope.
alternatives.outcome: The result reports the observed absence and scope without choosing or creating a change.

failures.condition: Configuration is invalid or a current candidate is malformed, ambiguous, unsupported, interrupted, or inaccessible.
failures.outcome: The system exposes the exact bounded problem and incomplete scope rather than hiding the candidate as archived.
The system reports the limit and incomplete scope without silently truncating or selecting an arbitrary candidate.

failures.condition: Operational history is absent or unavailable.
failures.outcome: The result identifies unavailable history; it neither claims no Changes exist nor initializes a new history through discovery.
